name: Dehiwala Zoo
blurb: The national zoo, one of the oldest in Asia, set in tropical gardens with a large aquarium, a butterfly park and a reptile house.

name: Galle Face Green
blurb: A long seafront lawn in central Colombo where families fly kites, eat street food and watch the sun set over the Indian Ocean.

name: Gangaramaya Temple
blurb: A busy Colombo temple mixing Sri Lankan, Thai, Indian and Chinese styles, with a museum crammed with gifts from devotees.

name: Independence Memorial Hall
blurb: A large open pavilion built to mark independence in 1948, modelled on Kandyan royal architecture and set in wide grounds for walking.

name: Jami Ul-Alfar Mosque
blurb: A red and white striped mosque in Pettah built in 1909, one of the most photographed buildings in Colombo.

name: Kelaniya Raja Maha Vihara
blurb: A major Buddhist temple on the Kelani River east of Colombo, known for its painted murals and the Duruthu perahera procession each January.

name: Lotus Tower
blurb: A 350-metre telecoms tower shaped like a lotus bud, with an observation deck over the city and the coast. It is lit up in colour at night.

image.commons_file: File:Lotus Tower Floating Market-Colombo Srilanka-Andres Larin.jpg
image.author: Saaremees

name: National Museum of Colombo
blurb: The country's largest museum, in a white colonial building, with royal regalia, ancient sculpture, masks and old maps.

name: Pettah Market
blurb: A crowded grid of streets where each lane sells something different, from spices and fabric to electronics. Busiest on weekday mornings.

image.commons_file: File:Bags of Spices in Market - Pettah District - Colombo - Sri Lanka (13995169756).jpg
image.author: Adam Jones from Kelowna, BC, Canada

name: Seema Malakaya
blurb: A small meditation hall on platforms in Beira Lake designed by Geoffrey Bawa, linked to the shore by a footbridge and lined with Buddha statues.

name: Viharamahadevi Park
blurb: Colombo's largest public park, facing the white Town Hall, with shady lawns, a large Buddha statue and fountains.

name: Barberyn Lighthouse
blurb: An 1889 lighthouse on a small island off Beruwala, seen from the beach or close up on a short boat trip from the fishing harbour.

name: Bolgoda Lake
blurb: The largest natural lake in Sri Lanka, a maze of wetland channels south of Colombo used for boat trips, birdwatching and rowing.

name: Hamilton Canal
blurb: A Dutch-era canal running south from Negombo, explored by boat or bicycle past fishing villages, mangroves and coconut groves.

name: Kalpitiya Dolphin Watching and Bar Reef
blurb: Boats from Kalpitiya head out from November to April to see large pods of spinner dolphins, with snorkelling on the Bar Reef nearby.

image.commons_file: File:Swiming With The Pod - Spinner dolphins in Kalpitiya.jpg
image.author: Woshitha

name: Kalpitiya Fort
blurb: A small coral-stone Dutch fort from the 1670s on the lagoon shore in Kalpitiya town, with a gateway and old walls. It sits on a naval base.

name: Kalpitiya Lagoon Kitesurfing
blurb: Flat, shallow water and steady wind make the Kalpitiya lagoon a top spot to learn kitesurfing, with the main season from May to October.

name: Kalutara Bodhiya and Chaitya
blurb: A large hollow white stupa beside the Kalu River bridge that you can walk inside, with murals of the Buddha's life around the inner wall.

name: Kande Viharaya
blurb: A hilltop temple near Aluthgama with a seated Buddha statue about 48 metres high, one of the tallest in the country, and an old stupa.

name: Kechimalai Mosque
blurb: A white mosque on a headland at Beruwala, built near the place where Arab traders are said to have first settled on the island.

name: Mount Lavinia Beach
blurb: A city beach south of Colombo below the colonial Mount Lavinia Hotel, with seafood restaurants on the sand and trains passing behind.

name: Muthurajawela Marsh
blurb: A large coastal wetland between Colombo and Negombo, explored by small boat to see water birds, monitor lizards and macaques.

name: Negombo Beach
blurb: A long beach close to the airport, lined with hotels and seafood restaurants, where outrigger fishing boats come in on the sand.

name: Negombo Fish Market
blurb: A busy early-morning market at Lellama where the night's catch is sold, with fish laid out to dry on mats along the beach nearby.

name: Negombo Fort
blurb: The remains of a Dutch fort from the 1670s by the lagoon mouth, with a gateway and a clock tower still standing. Part of it is a prison.

name: Negombo Lagoon
blurb: A wide estuary south of Negombo where you can take a boat past mangroves and fishermen working with traditional nets.

name: Richmond Castle
blurb: An early 1900s country mansion near Kalutara mixing Indian and British styles, with teak staircases, stained glass and large gardens.

name: St Anne's Church, Talawila
blurb: A seaside Catholic shrine on the Kalpitiya peninsula that draws large crowds of pilgrims for its feasts in March and July.

name: St Mary's Church, Negombo
blurb: A large Catholic church built between 1874 and 1922, with a tall facade and painted ceilings showing scenes from the Bible.

name: Wilpattu National Park
blurb: Sri Lanka's largest national park, a quiet mix of forest and natural lakes called villus, known for leopards and sloth bears.

image.commons_file: File:Sambar Deer at Wilpattu National Park.jpg
image.author: Manelka Jayasundara

name: Ariyapala Mask Museum
blurb: A family workshop and museum in Ambalangoda showing the carved and painted wooden masks used in southern dance, drama and healing rituals.

name: Bentota Beach
blurb: A long, wide beach on a sand spit between the Bentota River and the sea, used for swimming in the dry season and water sports on the river.

name: Brief Garden
blurb: The hillside garden of landscape designer Bevis Bawa, brother of Geoffrey, with winding paths, statues and a house hung with art.

name: Coconut Tree Hill
blurb: A small headland at the east end of Mirissa covered in tall coconut palms, with views over the bay. Best early morning or at sunset.

image.commons_file: File:View from Coconut Tree Hill to Mirissa in March.jpg
image.author: Alexey Komarov

name: Dalawella Beach
blurb: A palm-lined beach just east of Unawatuna with a natural rock pool, a well-known rope swing and turtles often feeding near the reef.

name: Dondra Head Lighthouse
blurb: Sri Lanka's tallest lighthouse, built in the late 1880s near the island's southern tip. Visitors can usually climb to the top for a small fee.

name: Galle Fort
blurb: A walled Dutch-era town on a headland. Walk the ramparts at sunset, then wander lanes of colonial houses, churches, cafés and small shops.

name: Galle Lighthouse
blurb: The white lighthouse on the south-east corner of the fort walls, dating from 1939. A good spot to watch waves break on the reef below.

name: Goyambokka Beach
blurb: A sheltered cove just west of Tangalle with soft sand and fairly calm water, good for a swim when the sea is settled.

name: Hikkaduwa Coral Reef
blurb: A shallow marine park off Hikkaduwa where you can snorkel or ride a glass-bottom boat over the reef, with green turtles feeding near the shore.

name: Hikkaduwa Main Reef
blurb: Hikkaduwa's best-known wave, a reef break off the main beach for intermediate surfers, with gentler beach breaks further south at Narigama.

name: Hiriketiya Bay
blurb: A small horseshoe bay with a reef break on one side and a mellow beach break on the other, ringed by palms and cafés.

name: Hummanaya Blowhole
blurb: A blowhole on a rocky headland near Kudawella that sends spray high into the air, strongest during the south-west monsoon from June to August.

name: Japanese Peace Pagoda, Rumassala
blurb: A white stupa built by Japanese Buddhist monks on Rumassala hill, looking back across the water to Galle Fort. Quiet in the early morning.

name: Jungle Beach
blurb: A small cove at the foot of Rumassala hill, reached on a forest path or by boat from Unawatuna, with clear water and coral close to shore.

name: Kabalana Beach, Ahangama
blurb: Ahangama's main surf beach. A reef break known as The Rock holds bigger swell, while softer waves on the inside suit learners.

name: Kalametiya Bird Sanctuary
blurb: A coastal lagoon and mangrove sanctuary near Hungama. Early boat trips show herons, kingfishers, painted storks and the odd crocodile.

name: Koggala Lake
blurb: A shallow lagoon scattered with small islands. Boat trips pass through mangroves to a cinnamon island and a temple on another island.

name: Kosgoda Turtle Hatchery
blurb: A beachside hatchery that buys turtle eggs from local collectors, reburies them in protected sand and releases the hatchlings into the sea.

name: Lunuganga
blurb: The country estate of architect Geoffrey Bawa, a landscaped garden of lawns, terraces and sculptures on Dedduwa Lake, shown on guided tours.

name: Madu Ganga
blurb: A mangrove-lined river estuary near Balapitiya with more than 60 islands, toured by boat to see cinnamon peeling and a small island temple.

name: Martin Wickramasinghe Folk Museum
blurb: The childhood home of the Sinhala novelist, now a museum of village life with old tools, masks, carts and household objects in a shady garden.

name: Midigama Surf Breaks
blurb: A row of reef breaks, among them Lazy Left and Rams, that suit intermediate and experienced surfers during the November to April season.

name: Mirissa Beach
blurb: A curved bay of soft sand sloping into clear water, with beach restaurants along the back and calm swimming in the dry months.

name: Mirissa Harbour (Whale Watching)
blurb: The fishing harbour where whale-watching boats leave at dawn from November to April, with blue whales and spinner dolphins often seen offshore.

name: Mulkirigala Rock Temple
blurb: A rock outcrop with cave temples on several levels, climbed by around 500 steps, with reclining Buddhas, murals and views over paddy fields.

name: Paravi Duwa Temple
blurb: A Buddhist temple on a small rocky island just off Matara beach, reached by a suspension footbridge. Popular with families in the evening.

name: Polhena Beach
blurb: A reef-protected beach near Matara with a shallow lagoon for snorkelling, where green turtles often feed close to the shore.

name: Rekawa Turtle Watch
blurb: A community project on Rekawa beach where guides take small groups out at night to watch green turtles come ashore to lay their eggs.

name: Star Fort, Matara
blurb: A small star-shaped Dutch fort from the 1760s on the edge of Matara, with a moat, a carved gateway and a small museum inside.

name: Stilt Fishermen, Koggala
blurb: Fishermen perched on poles set into the shallows between Koggala and Ahangama, a traditional method now mostly seen around dawn and dusk.

image.commons_file: File:Fishermen practicing traditional stilt fishing near Galle, southern Sri Lanka, 20260207 1420 9468.jpg
image.author: Jakub Hałun

name: Talalla Beach
blurb: A quiet crescent bay between Matara and Dickwella with gentle beginner waves, a few guesthouses and very little traffic.

name: Taprobane Island
blurb: A tiny rocky island in Weligama Bay topped by a villa built by a French count in the 1920s. You can wade out to it at low tide.

image.commons_file: File:TAPROBANE ISLAND NEAR KOGGLA SRI LANKA JAN 2013 (8491428227).jpg
image.author: calflier001

name: Unawatuna Beach
blurb: A curved, reef-sheltered bay with calm water for much of the dry season, good for swimming and snorkelling, backed by beach restaurants.

name: Ussangoda National Park
blurb: A clifftop plateau of red soil and low scrub above the sea, protected as a national park and linked in local legend to the Ramayana.

name: Weherahena Temple
blurb: A temple east of Matara with a giant seated Buddha and a long tunnel underground, its walls painted with scenes from the Buddha's lives.

name: Weligama Bay
blurb: A wide sandy bay with gentle, consistent beach-break waves, one of the most popular places in Sri Lanka to learn to surf.

name: Wewurukannala Vihara
blurb: A temple near Dickwella with a 50-metre seated Buddha and a hall of painted statues showing scenes of reward and punishment after death.

name: Gongala Mountain
blurb: The highest point of the Rakwana hills east of Deniyaya, climbed on a steep trail through forest and tea for wide views over Sinharaja and the south.

image.commons_file: File:Gongala Mountain view from Godawela area.jpg
image.author: Hashanhatharasinge

name: Kanneliya Forest Reserve
blurb: A protected lowland rainforest inland from Galle, with marked trails to streams, natural pools and waterfalls among tall trees.

name: Maduwanwela Walawwa
blurb: A manor house of a family of local chiefs near Kolonne, begun around 1700, with inner courtyards, period furniture and tiled floors, open as a museum.

name: Sinharaja Forest Reserve
blurb: A UNESCO-listed lowland rainforest. Guided walks from the Deniyaya side follow streams to waterfalls, with endemic birds, frogs and lizards.

name: Bundala National Park
blurb: A park of lagoons, scrub and dunes near Hambantota, best for birdwatching, with flamingos in some winters, crocodiles and occasional elephants.

image.commons_file: File:Painted Stork at Bundala National Park.jpg
image.author: Manelka Jayasundara

name: Elephant Transit Home
blurb: A rehabilitation centre for orphaned elephant calves beside Udawalawe park, where visitors watch the scheduled milk feeds from a platform.

name: Kataragama Temple
blurb: A sacred complex shared by Buddhists, Hindus and Muslims, busiest at the evening puja and during the July and August festival.

name: Kiri Vehera
blurb: A white stupa at the end of the Kataragama sacred road, believed to date to the 1st century BC, where pilgrims gather at dusk.

name: Kirinda Temple
blurb: A small temple on a boulder above Kirinda's fishing village, with a stupa at the top and views over the beach towards the Yala coast.

name: Lunugamvehera National Park
blurb: A quieter park north of Tissamaharama around a large reservoir, linking Yala and Udawalawe, with elephants, water birds and few other jeeps.

name: Sithulpawwa Rock Temple
blurb: An ancient monastery on a rock in the Yala forest, once home to thousands of monks, with a stupa on the summit and cave shrines below.

name: Tissa Wewa
blurb: An ancient reservoir on the edge of Tissamaharama, with a lakeside road for evening walks and good birdwatching among the dead trees.

name: Tissamaharama Raja Maha Vihara
blurb: A large white stupa first built more than 2,000 years ago by the kings of Ruhuna, still a busy place of worship near the town's reservoir.

name: Udawalawe National Park
blurb: Open grassland around a large reservoir where herds of elephants are seen on almost every jeep safari, along with buffalo, deer and eagles.

name: Udawalawe Reservoir
blurb: The large reservoir at the heart of Udawalawe park, with a road along the dam wall that gives views over the water and the hills beyond.

name: Yala National Park
blurb: Sri Lanka's best-known park for leopards, with elephants, sloth bears, crocodiles and birds. Jeep safaris enter through the Palatupana gate.

name: Aberdeen Falls
blurb: A 98-metre waterfall near Ginigathena, reached by a short walk down through forest to a wide pool at its foot.

name: Adam's Peak (Sri Pada)
blurb: A 2,243-metre sacred mountain climbed overnight by thousands of steps from Nallathanniya, timed to reach the top for sunrise. Season is December to May.

name: Adisham Bungalow
blurb: A 1930s English country house near Haputale, now a Benedictine monastery, with gardens and a small shop selling the monks' jams.

name: Ambuluwawa Tower
blurb: A spiral tower on a hilltop near Gampola, with a narrow outdoor staircase that climbs to wide views over the central hills.

name: Bahirawakanda Buddha Statue
blurb: A large white seated Buddha on a hilltop above Kandy, reached by a steep climb, with views over the city and the lake.

name: Bambarakanda Falls
blurb: Sri Lanka's tallest waterfall at 263 metres, falling down a sheer cliff among pine trees near Kalupahana. A short walk leads to the base.

name: Belilena Cave
blurb: A large rock cave near Kitulgala where remains of people who lived tens of thousands of years ago were found, reached by a forest path.

name: Castlereagh Reservoir
blurb: A long reservoir among tea estates near Hatton and Norwood, with lakeside bungalows, walking paths and views of Adam's Peak.

name: Ceylon Tea Museum
blurb: A former tea factory in the Hantana hills with old machinery, displays on the history of Ceylon tea and a tasting room with views.

name: Degaldoruwa Cave Temple
blurb: An 18th-century cave temple near Kandy with some of the best-preserved Kandyan wall paintings, showing stories of the Buddha's past lives.

name: Demodara Loop
blurb: A railway spiral where the line loops round a hill and passes under itself to reach Demodara station, a feat of colonial engineering.

name: Devon Falls
blurb: A 97-metre waterfall named after an early coffee planter, seen from a roadside viewpoint on the main road near Talawakele.

name: Diyaluma Falls
blurb: A 220-metre waterfall near Koslanda. A trail climbs to natural rock pools at the top where you can swim, with views over the plains.

name: Dowa Rock Temple
blurb: A temple in a cave by a stream between Ella and Bandarawela, with an unfinished standing Buddha carved into the rock face.

name: Dunhinda Falls
blurb: A waterfall near Badulla that throws off a fine mist, reached on a path of about 1 km with views over the river valley.

name: Ella Rock
blurb: A steeper half-day hike from Ella along the railway line and through tea and eucalyptus to a cliff edge looking over the lowlands.

name: Embekke Devalaya
blurb: A 14th-century shrine known for the carved wooden pillars of its drumming hall, decorated with dancers, wrestlers, birds and animals.

name: Gadaladeniya Temple
blurb: A 14th-century stone temple on a rock outcrop near Kandy, built in a south Indian style with carved doorways and a small stupa.

name: Hakgala Botanical Garden
blurb: A cool hill garden below Hakgala rock with rose gardens, ferns, conifers and monkeys, first planted in the 1860s to grow cinchona.

name: Horton Plains and World's End
blurb: A high plateau of grassland and cloud forest. A 9 km loop walk leads to the World's End cliff and Baker's Falls. Go early before the mist rises.

image.commons_file: File:World's End, Horton Plains National Park, Sri Lanka.jpg
image.author: Sendaru Perera

name: Hunnas Falls
blurb: A waterfall in the tea country near Elkaduwa, north of Kandy, set among plantations with walking paths through the estate.

name: Kandy Lake
blurb: An artificial lake built by the last king of Kandy in 1807, with a shady path around it about 3 km long and views of the Temple of the Tooth.

name: Kandy Municipal Market
blurb: A covered market around a courtyard in central Kandy selling fruit, spices, tea, batik and handicrafts.

image.commons_file: File:Spice shop in Kandy Market, Sri Lanka.jpg
image.author: McKay Savage

name: Kelani River Rafting
blurb: Kitulgala's stretch of the Kelani River has grade 2 to 3 rapids, run by rafting operators on half-day trips through the forest.

name: Knuckles Mountain Range
blurb: A UNESCO-listed range of misty peaks, cloud forest and small villages north-east of Kandy, explored on guided day hikes and treks.

name: Lake Gregory
blurb: A reservoir at the edge of Nuwara Eliya with a lakeside park, pedal boats, pony rides and a walking path around the shore.

name: Lankatilaka Temple
blurb: A tall 14th-century temple on a rocky hill near Kandy with old paintings, a seated Buddha and views across the countryside.

name: Laxapana Falls
blurb: A waterfall about 126 metres high on the Maskeliya Oya near Norton Bridge, reached by a short walk down through village paths.

name: Lipton's Seat
blurb: A lookout at the top of the Dambatenne tea estate where Thomas Lipton surveyed his land. Arrive early for views across several provinces.

name: Little Adam's Peak
blurb: An easy walk of about 45 minutes from Ella through tea gardens to a grassy summit with views down the Ella Gap.

image.commons_file: File:Little Adam's Peak, Ella, Sri Lanka.jpg
image.author: Bcd4e6

name: Mackwoods Labookellie Tea Centre
blurb: A tea centre on the winding Ramboda road where you can walk through the factory and have tea and cake overlooking the estate.

name: Maussakelle Reservoir
blurb: A reservoir in the hills below Adam's Peak, passed on the road to Nallathanniya, with tea estates running down to the water.

name: Moon Plains
blurb: A grassland reserve above Nuwara Eliya with a viewpoint that, on clear mornings, shows several of the island's highest peaks.

name: Muthiyangana Raja Maha Vihara
blurb: An ancient Buddhist temple in the centre of Badulla, with a white stupa and painted shrine rooms, said to be visited by the Buddha.

name: Nine Arch Bridge
blurb: A stone railway viaduct with nine arches set in jungle and tea near Ella. Locals post the train times, so you can watch one cross.

name: Nuwara Eliya Post Office
blurb: A red-brick Tudor-style post office from 1894 in the town centre, still in use and a reminder of the town's colonial hill-station past.

name: Pedro Tea Estate
blurb: A working tea factory just outside Nuwara Eliya that runs short tours of the withering and rolling floors, followed by a tea tasting.

name: Ramboda Falls
blurb: A 109-metre waterfall beside the Kandy to Nuwara Eliya road, with a path from the hotel above down to the base of the falls.

name: Ravana Falls
blurb: A tiered waterfall beside the Ella to Wellawaya road, about 25 metres high, flowing strongest in the rainy months.

name: Royal Botanic Gardens, Peradeniya
blurb: A large botanic garden on a bend of the Mahaweli River with an orchid house, a giant Javan fig tree, palm avenues and a long suspension bridge.

name: Samanalawewa Reservoir
blurb: A hydroelectric reservoir below Belihuloya, set in wooded hills, with views of the water from the dam road.

name: Seetha Amman Temple
blurb: A colourful Hindu temple by a stream near Hakgala, linked by tradition to the place where Sita was held in the Ramayana.

name: St. Clair's Falls
blurb: One of the widest waterfalls in Sri Lanka, falling in two tiers through tea estates. A tea lounge on the main road looks straight at it.

name: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
blurb: The temple in the old royal palace in Kandy that holds a relic of the Buddha's tooth. Visit at puja time to hear drums and see offerings.

image.commons_file: File:Sri Lanka, Kandy, Temple of the Tooth, Sri Dalada Maligawa.jpg
image.author: Vyacheslav Argenberg

name: Udawatta Kele Forest
blurb: A forest reserve on the hill behind the Temple of the Tooth, once the royal pleasure garden, with walking trails, monkeys and many birds.

name: Victoria Park, Nuwara Eliya
blurb: A tidy town park in the centre of Nuwara Eliya with flower beds, a stream and many birds, at its best from February to May.

name: Victoria Reservoir
blurb: A large reservoir in the hills east of Kandy, held back by a tall arch dam, with viewpoints over the water and surrounding forest.

name: Abhayagiri Monastery
blurb: The ruins of a large monastery in the north of Anuradhapura, with a restored brick stupa, guard stones, moonstones and a museum.

image.commons_file: File:Abhayagiri Dagoba in Anuradhapura, Sri Lanka.jpg
image.author: Nicolas Chadeville

name: Aluvihare Rock Temple
blurb: Cave temples among boulders north of Matale, where Buddhist teachings were first written down on palm leaves in the 1st century BC.

name: Ancient City of Polonnaruwa
blurb: The medieval royal capital, best seen by bicycle, with palace ruins, a circular relic house, stupas and temples spread across a large park.

image.commons_file: File:The Quadrangle Vatadage, Ancient City of Polonnaruwa, Sri Lanka (2).jpg
image.author: Nahid Sultan

name: Avukana Buddha Statue
blurb: A standing Buddha about 12 metres tall, carved from a granite rock face in the 5th century near the Kala Wewa reservoir.

name: Dambulla Cave Temple
blurb: Five painted caves high on a rock above Dambulla, filled with over 150 Buddha statues and ceiling murals, used for worship for 2,000 years.

image.commons_file: File:Statue of the Buddha reclining in the Dambulla cave temple, Dambulla, Sri Lanka, 20260201 1419 8127.jpg
image.author: Jakub Hałun

name: Gal Vihara
blurb: Four large Buddha figures cut into one granite rock face in Polonnaruwa in the 12th century, including a 14-metre reclining Buddha.

name: Hurulu Eco Park
blurb: A dry forest reserve near Habarana used for elephant safaris during the wet months, when the herds are less often at Minneriya.

image.commons_file: File:Hurulu Eco Park, North Central Province, Sri Lanka, 20260201 1032 7859.jpg
image.author: Jakub Hałun

name: Isurumuniya
blurb: A rock temple beside a pond in Anuradhapura, known for its carved lovers and elephant reliefs. Climb the rock at sunset.

name: Jaya Sri Maha Bodhi
blurb: A sacred fig tree in Anuradhapura grown from a cutting of the Bodhi tree in India, planted in 288 BC and visited by pilgrims every day.

name: Jetavanaramaya
blurb: A brick stupa from the 3rd century, once among the tallest buildings in the ancient world, surrounded by monastery ruins.

name: Kaudulla National Park
blurb: A park around another old reservoir near Habarana, often visited when the elephant herds move away from Minneriya.

name: Mihintale
blurb: A hill east of Anuradhapura where Buddhism is said to have been introduced to the island, climbed by a long stone stairway to stupas and views.

name: Minneriya National Park
blurb: A park around an ancient reservoir where hundreds of elephants gather in the dry season, roughly July to October, to graze on the shore.

name: Nalanda Gedige
blurb: A stone temple standing on its own by a reservoir near Matale, built in a mix of Hindu and Buddhist styles more than 1,000 years ago.

name: Parakrama Samudra
blurb: A vast reservoir built in the 12th century beside Polonnaruwa, with an embankment road that is good at sunset.

name: Pidurangala Rock
blurb: A rock just north of Sigiriya with a cave temple and a reclining Buddha. A short scramble to the top gives the best view of Sigiriya.

name: Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage
blurb: A government-run home for orphaned and injured elephants. The herd walks down to bathe in the Maha Oya river twice a day.

name: Ritigala Forest Monastery
blurb: Ruins of a forest monastery on a mountainside, with stone paths, bridges and meditation platforms among tall trees.

name: Riverston
blurb: A windy ridge in the Knuckles range above Matale with grassland walks, a viewpoint called Pitawala Pathana and small waterfalls nearby.

name: Ruwanwelisaya
blurb: A huge white stupa from the 2nd century BC, ringed by a wall of carved elephants. Pilgrims in white circle it in the evening.

name: Sigiriya Rock Fortress
blurb: A 5th-century palace on top of a 180-metre rock, climbed past water gardens, painted frescoes and giant stone lion paws.

name: Sri Muthumariamman Temple, Matale
blurb: A Hindu temple in Matale with a tall gopuram tower covered in painted figures of gods, busiest during the yearly chariot festival.

name: Arugam Bay Main Point
blurb: A long right-hand point break at the south end of the bay, one of the best-known waves in Sri Lanka, at its best from May to September.

name: Batticaloa Fort
blurb: A small Portuguese and Dutch fort on an island in the Batticaloa lagoon, with thick walls, old cannons and lagoon views.

name: Batticaloa Lagoon
blurb: A long lagoon running through Batticaloa, crossed by old bridges and known for its singing fish heard on still nights around the full moon.

name: Batticaloa Lighthouse
blurb: A 28-metre lighthouse from 1913 at the mouth of the Batticaloa lagoon, with a small park where locals gather in the evening.

name: Fort Frederick
blurb: A 17th-century fort on the Trincomalee headland, still an army base, which you pass through on the way to Koneswaram. Spotted deer roam inside.

name: Kalkudah Beach
blurb: A long, quiet beach just south of Pasikudah with fewer hotels, fishing boats on the sand and room for long walks.

name: Kallady Beach
blurb: A long, open beach across the lagoon bridge from Batticaloa town, quiet in the day and busy with local families at sunset.

name: Kanniya Hot Wells
blurb: Seven small square wells of warm spring water near Trincomalee, each a slightly different temperature, where visitors pour buckets over themselves.

name: Koneswaram Temple
blurb: A Hindu temple on the top of Swami Rock in Trincomalee, above sheer cliffs. Blue whales and dolphins are sometimes seen from the edge.

name: Kudumbigala Monastery
blurb: A forest hermitage of rock caves and ruins south of Arugam Bay. Climb the rock for views over forest and sea.

name: Kumana National Park
blurb: A remote park south of Arugam Bay with wetlands that fill with nesting water birds from April to July, plus elephants and leopards.

name: Lahugala Kitulana National Park
blurb: A small park inland from Pottuvil around a few reservoirs, where elephants often come out to feed on the tall grass in the dry season.

name: Marble Beach
blurb: A sheltered bay south of Trincomalee run by the air force, with very clear, calm water and a beach with simple facilities.

name: Muhudu Maha Viharaya
blurb: Ancient temple ruins among sand dunes on the beach at Pottuvil, with old Buddha statues looking out to sea.

name: Nilaveli Beach
blurb: A long, quiet beach of pale sand north of Trincomalee with calm water from May to September and boats to Pigeon Island.

name: Pasikudah Beach
blurb: A wide bay with a shallow, sandy shelf that stays waist deep a long way out, making it one of the calmest swimming beaches on the island.

name: Pigeon Island National Park
blurb: A small island off Nilaveli with a shallow coral reef. Boats take snorkellers to see reef fish, turtles and blacktip reef sharks.

name: Pottuvil Lagoon
blurb: A mangrove lagoon just north of Pottuvil, explored on short trips by traditional canoe to see birds, monkeys and crocodiles.

name: Trincomalee War Cemetery
blurb: A neatly kept Commonwealth cemetery for service people who died in and around Trincomalee during the Second World War.

name: Uppuveli Beach
blurb: A beach a few kilometres north of Trincomalee with guesthouses, restaurants and dive shops, calm and clear in the summer months.

image.author: Honeplus

name: Whiskey Point
blurb: A sandy right-hand point north of Pottuvil with softer, slower waves than Main Point, good for beginners and longboarders.

name: Casuarina Beach
blurb: A shallow, calm beach on Karainagar island, reached by causeway from Jaffna, named after the casuarina trees along the sand.

name: Jaffna Fort
blurb: A large star-shaped fort built by the Portuguese and rebuilt by the Dutch, with ramparts you can walk for views over the lagoon.

name: Jaffna Public Library
blurb: A white library in an Indo-Saracenic style, rebuilt after it was burnt in 1981 and an important symbol for the Tamil community.

name: Kadurugoda Temple
blurb: A cluster of small ancient stupas in Chunnakam, north of Jaffna, the remains of a Buddhist monastery from the early centuries AD.

name: Keerimalai Springs
blurb: Freshwater springs by the sea on the north coast, filled into stone bathing pools beside a Hindu temple. Locals come to swim.

name: Nainativu Island
blurb: A small island reached by ferry from Kurikadduwan, with both the Hindu Nagapooshani Amman temple and the Buddhist Nagadeepa Vihara.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Temple
blurb: Jaffna's largest Hindu temple, with a golden gopuram tower. Men remove their shirts to enter, and the 25-day festival takes place in August.
